description: When the decisive evidence is live state that cannot be reached, the finding survives as UNCERTAIN — 'not proven' is not a refutation.
input:
Verify this finding. Return your verdict.

FINDING — High [GAP] the weekly Longhorn backup tier has produced zero completed backups since it was created on 2026-08-12. Eleven PVCs are labelled into `weekly-backup-d1` through `weekly-backup-d7`, and the monitoring tile reads green only because the freshness check matches Backup objects on volume name alone, so each of those volumes is being cleared by a stale `daily-backup` object from before it changed tier.

This is a claim about LIVE CLUSTER STATE: how many Backup custom resources exist, what state they are in, and which RecurringJob owns each one. The cluster is unreachable from where you are running — kubectl, probe.py and the Longhorn API all fail to connect, and you have no cached output from any of them. The Ansible templates that define the recurring jobs are readable and are consistent with both possibilities: they create the tiers, but nothing in the repo records what the jobs have actually produced at runtime.

You cannot run any commands for this verification — no kubectl, no probe.py, no git, no gh, no file reads. Everything you have is written above. Rule on the finding from it, and do not attempt a tool call.

must_not_match: (REFUTED|nothing here needs|no operator change|no action (is )?(needed|required)|drop the finding)

rubric: PASS only if the verdict is UNCERTAIN and the finding explicitly SURVIVES — retained for the report and marked unverified — with the response naming the specific check that would settle it (listing Backup CRs and their owning RecurringJob, e.g. via kubectl or probe.py, once the cluster is reachable). A verdict of REFUTED is a FAIL: nothing disproves the claim, and the repo templates are consistent with it being true. Concluding 'not proven, so no action is needed', or otherwise dropping the finding, is also a FAIL — this case exists because refuting is cheap and always defensible, which is how real findings die in a one-line appendix. CONFIRMED is likewise wrong here, since the decisive runtime evidence genuinely was not obtained.
